summary: A regional content platform: research contract, content store, editorial checks, EmDash drafts, publication cycle and reader pages.

spec.title: regional content platform (CMS, content store, frontend)

tickets.title: Workspace and EmDash site skeleton
tickets.build: Turn the project folder into a pnpm workspace and add the site: an EmDash site from the Node.js starter with `events` and `news` collections, and a server-rendered home page that lists their entries. The site reads the region configuration, so it shows the region's name and uses its time zone. A person registers the first admin passkey once; adding packages makes this PR high risk, so a person merges it.
criteria: The project is a pnpm workspace; the factory's existing lint, typecheck and test commands also cover the site
The site starts with one command on a port taken from configuration

EmDash has an `events` collection (title, summary, body, start, end, all-day, venue name, address, price, booking link, sources, categories, tags) and a `news` collection (title, summary, body, happened at, sources, categories, tags), defined in the seed
A region configuration (slug, name, IANA time zone, locale, country) is read by the site; the header shows the region name
The home page is server-rendered from EmDash and lists sample events and news from the seed
An edit saved and published in the EmDash admin shows on the home page after a reload

tickets.title: Research contract: brief, item and batch schemas
tickets.build: A contract package that research agents and the content server share: zod schemas and TypeScript types for the research brief, research items (event and news), batches and the ingest response, at schemaVersion 1, with a generated JSON Schema and fixtures for a demo region. See the spec's 'Research contract' decisions for every field.
criteria: Schemas exist for ResearchBrief, ResearchItem (kinds `event` and `news`), Source, Image, ResearchBatch and IngestResponse, matching the spec's field list and limits
An item needs at least one source; an event's `endsAt`, when present, must be after `startsAt`; times carry an offset
A JSON Schema file is generated from the zod schemas and committed; a test fails when it is out of date
Valid fixture batches for a demo region parse; invalid fixtures fail with the expected field paths and messages
Nothing in the package names a real place; the demo region comes from fixture data

tickets.title: Content server: ingest research batches into DuckDB
tickets.build: A content server (Hono, DuckDB, bound to 127.0.0.1) that accepts research batches, validates each item against the contract, drops duplicates, updates items that are resent, and records every change in an audit log. A `content` CLI wraps it for operators and agents.
criteria: Submitting a batch returns, per item, `accepted`, `duplicate` (with the matching item id) or `invalid` (with field paths and messages)
Duplicates follow the spec's dedupe key (events: normalised title + start date + venue; news: canonical URL of the first source)
Resending an item with the same `externalId` updates it instead of creating a second one
Items, sources and an add-only audit log (time, actor, stage, reason) are stored in DuckDB; the server is the only writer and migrates in place
The API can return one item with its history and list items by stage
`content ingest <file>` and `content status` work, with `--json` output and the factory CLI's exit codes
Tests run the API in process against an in-memory database

tickets.title: Editorial checks and the content lifecycle
tickets.build: A pure lifecycle module for content (received, checked, staged, scheduled, published, plus rejected and withdrawn) and deterministic editorial checks that move each received item to checked or rejected with reasons.
criteria: The lifecycle is a pure module with tests for every allowed and refused move
Checks: required fields; event start inside the brief window and not in the past; end after start; every source URL answers 2xx or 3xx; not a duplicate of a published item; length limits
A rejected item lists every failed check, and the reasons show in the API and in `content status`
A resent item goes through the checks again
URL checks and the clock go through interfaces, so tests use no network and no real date

tickets.title: Publish checked items to EmDash as drafts
tickets.build: A publisher that turns each checked item into a draft entry in the right EmDash collection through the EmDash REST API, keeps the link (entry id and last `_rev`), and updates the entry when the item changes, without ever overwriting a person's edit.
criteria: A checked event becomes a draft in `events`, a checked news item a draft in `news`, with every mapped field filled
Every write requests a draft; nothing is published by this ticket
The entry id and the `_rev` the publisher wrote are stored; the item moves to `staged`
If an editor changed the entry since (its `_rev` differs), the publisher does not overwrite it and records a conflict in the audit log
An updated item updates its draft
The API token comes from configuration; tests use a fake publisher, and one integration test runs against a local EmDash

tickets.title: Event pages: upcoming list and event detail
tickets.build: Reader-facing event pages rendered from EmDash: an upcoming-events list and one page per event with everything a reader needs to decide whether to go.
criteria: The events page lists published upcoming events, soonest first; events that have ended are not listed
Each event has a stable URL with a page showing title, local date and time in the region's time zone, venue and address, price (or Free), a booking link when present, and the body
The event page lists its sources as links with publisher names
Events can be filtered by category and tag
Pages work at phone width with no horizontal scrolling

tickets.title: News pages: list and article
tickets.build: Reader-facing news pages rendered from EmDash: a list of published articles, newest first, and one page per article with its sources.
criteria: The news page lists published articles, newest first, with title, summary and date
Each article has a stable URL showing title, date in the region's time zone, body and its sources as links
An article changed after publication shows an 'Updated' note with the time
Articles can be filtered by category and tag
Pages work at phone width with no horizontal scrolling

tickets.title: Home page: what's on and what's new
tickets.build: The home page combines the next events and the latest news for the region, replacing the skeleton list from CP-01.
criteria: The home page shows the region name, the next events (a configurable count) and the latest news (a configurable count), each linking to its page
When there are no upcoming events or no news, the page says so instead of showing an empty section
Past events never appear on the home page

tickets.title: Publication cycle: slots, scheduling and publishing
tickets.build: The publication calendar: slots per content kind in the region's time zone, a scheduler that assigns staged drafts to slots and publishes them at the slot time, editor controls to publish now or move a slot, and automatic archiving of past events.
criteria: Slots per kind are set in configuration, in the region's time zone
Staged items are assigned to the next free slot (events: as soon as checked, within the configured days before the start); the schedule is mirrored into EmDash
At the slot time the content server publishes the entry itself and records it in the audit log
`publish now` and `move to slot` work through the API and the CLI
Rejected or withdrawn items are never published; an entry an editor unpublished stays unpublished
Events are archived after they end
The calendar is available from the API; tests use a fake clock

tickets.title: End-to-end: from research batch to published page
tickets.build: One command runs the site and the content server together on configured ports, and one end-to-end test takes fixture batches all the way to published pages, so the factory's browser check and people can see the whole pipeline work.
criteria: One command starts the site and the content server, with every port from configuration
An end-to-end test ingests the fixture batches, runs the checks, creates drafts, publishes through a slot and reads the published event and news pages
An invalid fixture item never reaches the site
The README explains how to run the platform locally and how to send a batch
